questions.question: Mayurbhanj Chhau dance is native to which state?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mayurbhanj Chhau is a traditional dance form that originated in the Mayurbhanj district of Odisha.
 
• It is one of the three forms of Chhau dance, the other two being Seraikella Chhau of Jharkhand and Purulia Chhau of West Bengal.
 
• This dance form is known for its vigorous martial movements and intricate footwork, which are inspired by the martial arts traditions of the region.
 
• Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed during various festivals and occasions, most notably during the Chaitra Parva festival, which is celebrated in the month of April.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau Dance:**

 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance with martial, tribal, and folk traditions, with origins in eastern India.
 
• It is performed in the states of Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal and is recognized as an intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO.
 
• The dance incorporates masks in the Seraikella and Purulia styles, while the Mayurbhanj style does not use masks.
 
• Chhau dance themes often revolve around mythological stories, epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, and local folklore.
 
 
 
• **Chaitra Parva:**
 
 
• Chaitra Parva is a significant festival in Odisha, celebrated in the month of Chaitra (March-April) according to the Hindu calendar.
 
• It marks the beginning of the new year for the tribal communities in the region and is celebrated with great enthusiasm.
 
• The festival is known for its vibrant cultural performances, including the Chhau dance, which is a major highlight.
 
• People from various communities come together to participate in the festivities, showcasing their rich cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Martial Arts Influence:**
 
 
• Mayurbhanj Chhau dance is heavily influenced by the martial arts traditions of the region, incorporating dynamic movements and acrobatics.
 
• Performers often undergo rigorous training to master the techniques and physical prowess required for the dance.
 
• The dance movements depict various aspects of martial arts, including combat techniques, weapon usage, and defensive stances.
 
• This influence adds a unique and energetic dimension to the Mayurbhanj Chhau dance, setting it apart from other dance forms.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• In 2010, Chhau dance was inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO.
 
• This recognition highlights the cultural significance and unique heritage of the Chhau dance tradition.
 
• UNESCO's recognition helps in preserving and promoting the art form, ensuring its continuation for future generations.
 
• It also brings international attention to the rich cultural diversity and artistic expressions of India.

In __**1667 AD**__ Francois Caron establish First French Factory in India. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In 1667 AD, **François Caron**, a Dutch-born merchant who was working for the French East India Company, established the first French factory in India. 
 
• The factory was located in **Surat,** a **major port city in Gujarat**. 
 
• This was the beginning of French colonial expansion in India, which would eventually lead to the establishment of French India.
 
• The factory in Surat was a success, and it helped to pave the way for the establishment of other French factories in India. 
 
• In **1669**, another French factory was established in Masulipatnam, a port city in **Andhra Pradesh. **
 
• In 1673, the French East India Company established a trading post in **Pondicherry,** which would eventually become the capital of French India.
 
• The French East India Company was one of the three major European trading companies that competed for control of trade in India during the **17th and 18th centuries.** 
 
• The other two companies were the **Dutch East India Company and the British East India Company. **
 
• The French company was never as successful as the British company, but it did manage to establish a number of colonies in India, including **Pondicherry, Chandannagar, and Mahé.**
 
• The French colonies in India were eventually annexed by the British during the 19th century. 
 
• 
 
However, the French legacy can still be seen in India today, in the form of French-style architecture, French cuisine, and the French language.

 

Therefore the correct answer is **1667 AD.**

__**Seasonal difference in temperature:**__

__
 
• **The axial tilt of the earth of 23.5 degrees as it moves around the sun causes seasonal changes.**
 
• The sunlight intensity on some parts of the earth significantly varies over the course of the year as the earth changes its orientation in space. 
 
• Seasonal variation in solar input occurs because **the Earth is tilted on its axis by 23.5˚** (Figure 2). 
 
• As Earth orbits the sun, its orientation to the sun changes.
 
• When in June the northern hemisphere tills toward the sun it gets maximum heat while the southern hemisphere gets little heat.
 
• It is the summer in the Northern hemisphere and winter in the southern hemisphere.
 
• 6 months later in December, the situation is reversed and the earth Travels half around the Sun, and in the Northern hemisphere is tilted away from the sun.
 
• On June 21 the sun is directly overhead the Tropic of Cancer and it is mid-summer in the Northern hemisphere.
 
• Midsummer in the southern hemisphere occurs on 23rd December when the sun is directly overhead the Tropic of Capricorn.

***The rotation of the earth is the main cause of the day-night phenomena. The circle that divides the day from night on the globe is called the circle of illumination. ***

questions.question: Under Article 239 of the Constitution, a Union Territory is administered by:

options.text: the Governor of an adjacent State

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under **Article 239** of the Constitution of India, Union Territories are administered by the President of India through an administrator appointed by him/her.
 
• The President appoints an administrator or Lieutenant Governor for each Union Territory, who acts as the executive head of the Union Territory.
 
• The **President** of India has the ultimate authority over Union Territories, making administrative decisions and delegating powers to the appointed administrators.
 
• Union Territories are governed directly by the **Central Government** unlike states which have their own elected governments. This ensures a centralized form of administration.
 
• **Examples:** Union Territories like Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir have a special status with elected legislative assemblies, but their administrators still report to the President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union Territories of India:**

 
 
• India currently has **8 Union Territories**, including Delhi, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Ladakh, and Jammu & Kashmir.
 
• They are directly governed by the **Central Government**, unlike states which have their own governments.
 
• Some Union Territories, like Delhi and Puducherry, have legislative assemblies but their powers are limited compared to states.
 
 
 
• **Role of Administrator/Lieutenant Governor:**
 
 
• Administrators or Lieutenant Governors act as the representatives of the **President of India** in Union Territories.
 
• They oversee the administration, law enforcement, and implementation of policies directly from the **Union Government**.
 
• In Union Territories with legislative assemblies, the administrator/Lieutenant Governor acts in coordination with the elected government but retains significant powers.
 
 
 
• **Article 239:**
 
 
• Article 239 provides the constitutional framework for the governance of Union Territories.
 
• The **President** may appoint an administrator for Union Territories or delegate certain powers to the administrator for efficient administration.
 
• The administrator functions under the President's direct supervision and guidance.
 
 
 
• **Special Status Union Territories:**
 
 
• Union Territories like **Delhi** and **Puducherry** have legislative assemblies, allowing them to make laws on certain subjects.
 
• However, the administrator/Lieutenant Governor plays a critical role as they act on behalf of the President and can override decisions in specific circumstances.
 
• The governance of these Union Territories is a unique blend of centralized and decentralized administration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Union Territories without Legislative Assemblies:**

 
 
• Union Territories like **Chandigarh**, **Lakshadweep**, and **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** are governed entirely by administrators appointed by the President without any legislative assembly.
 
• Their policies and administration are directly influenced by the **Central Government**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Central Government:**
 
 
• The Union Territories are supervised and funded by the **Union Government**, ensuring uniform administration across the country.
 
• They are often used as strategic locations for governance, security, and development purposes.
 
 
 
• **Governance Framework:**
 
 
• The governance of Union Territories follows a centralized approach but ensures flexibility for those with legislative assemblies like Delhi and Puducherry.
 
• This framework allows the President to maintain control while delegating administrative powers to local representatives.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Union Territories were created to ensure efficient governance of regions that were either too small to be states or had strategic importance.
 
• Examples include **Chandigarh**, a planned city serving as the capital of two states (Punjab and Haryana).

questions.question: Which institution has published the Human Development Report annually since 1990?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP):**

 
 
• The UNDP has been publishing the **Human Development Report** annually since 1990.
 
• The report was introduced to shift the focus of development economics from national income as the sole indicator of development to a broader analysis of human well-being.
 
• The Human Development Report is best known for introducing the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, which measures countries' performance across three dimensions:
 
 
• Health (life expectancy at birth).
 
• Education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling).
 
• Standard of living (gross national income per capita).
 
 
 
• The objective of the report is to emphasize the importance of expanding people’s choices and enhancing their capabilities to lead meaningful lives.
 
• These reports are globally influential and serve as a crucial tool for policymakers, researchers, and governments to address pressing development challenges.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Bank:**

 
 
• The World Bank is a global financial institution that provides loans and grants to developing countries for development projects aimed at reducing poverty.
 
• While the World Bank produces several key reports, such as the **World Development Report**, it does not publish the Human Development Report.
 
• The focus of the World Bank is more on economic development and infrastructure projects, rather than the broader human development focus of the UNDP.
 
 
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF):**
 
 
• The IMF is primarily concerned with global monetary cooperation, financial stability, and the facilitation of international trade.
 
• Its major publications, such as the **World Economic Outlook**, focus on macroeconomic analysis, financial stability, and global economic trends.
 
• Unlike the UNDP, the IMF does not focus on human development or produce reports related to the HDI or other developmental indicators.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP):**
 
 
• The UNEP focuses on environmental issues and sustainability, aiming to provide leadership and encourage partnerships for protecting the environment.
 
• Its notable reports include the **Global Environment Outlook** and assessments on climate change, biodiversity, and resource management.
 
• While environmental sustainability is a component of human development, the UNEP does not produce the Human Development Report, as its primary focus lies elsewhere.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The first Human Development Report, published in 1990, was authored by economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen**.
 
• The concept of human development introduced by the report emphasized the significance of expanding human freedoms and well-being, rather than focusing solely on economic growth.
 
• The Human Development Report also addresses pressing issues like inequality, gender equity, climate change, and access to basic services.
 
• Over the years, the report has evolved to include additional indices, such as the **Gender Development Index (GDI)**, **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, and **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**, to provide a more nuanced understanding of human development.
 
• The Human Development Report serves as a critical tool for measuring progress, advocating for policy changes, and raising awareness about key global challenges.
